note: SNCF Intercités de Nuit, keyed the way the feed actually identifies trains. The first probe round assumed endpoint pairs and route names; both were wrong — see `disproved` below. The feed leaves trip_short_name empty on all 43,425 trips and carries the train number in trip_headsign, and its 711 routes are TER/Intercités lines ('P53', 'Bening - Sarreguemines') with not one mentioning 'nuit'. So the adapter selects by number, guarded by the objective overnight test in overnightTrips() (scripts/lib/gtfs.mjs): stop_times crossing midnight, >= 7h, route_type=2.
selectionRule: Every number Back-on-Track already lists is included unconditionally — those are the rows being enriched, and a pure trip-count threshold would have dropped two of them: BoT runs Paris–Aurillac as 3789/3790 (2 trips each in the feed) while the feed's dominant number on that corridor is 3792 (6 trips). Beyond those, a feed number is included when it runs >= 4 times in the ~160-day window, which is what separates a scheduled service from a one-off relief.
portionSplit: Rows 109 and 119 both carry 3754/3755 — L'Occitan splits into Albi and Rodez portions, and the feed carries both under the same number (Rodez modal at 8 dates, Albi at 3). Keyed by number alone the Rodez data would land on the Albi row, so the adapter disambiguates on `endpoint` and emits the exact `botKeys` string each row expects. That is also why 109's keys carry the '(Sun)' suffix: enrich.trainsByNumber does an exact lookup on trip_short_name.

observedNotMapped.note: Night trains the feed carries that are not built into map routes, with their trip counts over the ~160-day window. Recorded rather than dropped silently: if any of these grows into a scheduled service, it belongs in trainNumbers.
observedNotMapped.reason: 5741/5744/5787/3795 are one-off or relief workings on corridors already covered by their scheduled number. The 64001–64006 block runs Paris↔Briançon once each with 6–7 stops, which does not look like a public timetable entry; what it actually is has not been established.

disproved.note: Kept so the next national feed does not repeat the experiment.
disproved.endpointPairs: Matching { from: 'Paris', to: <city> } built 13 'sleeper' routes instead of 9, four of them daytime TGV sharing a city pair (Paris Montparnasse → Tarbes, Gare de Lyon → Nice). 'Paris – Rodez' matched nothing.
disproved.routeNames: buildSleeperTrains groups by route_id and emits one train per route. Here one route_id bundles several corridors — the 'Paris - Latour-de-Carol' route's representative trip runs Albi → Paris.
disproved.tripShortName: Empty on all 43,425 trips. Round 1 reported all sixteen numbers 'NOT FOUND' because it read this field; they are all present in trip_headsign.
